title: What If You Released 102 Toads in a New Country?

scenes.text: What if you released 102 toads to fight a beetle? Eighty years later, they'd be a billion-strong problem.
In 1935, Australia did exactly that. Toads from Hawaii were set loose in Queensland to eat sugar cane beetles.
The toads ignored the beetles. There is no evidence they changed beetle numbers at all.
By 1984 they had crossed into the Northern Territory. Today the front moves roughly 40 to 60 kilometers every year.
Their skin glands carry poison. Northern quolls and some monitor lizards collapsed, and local goanna numbers fell by up to 90 percent.
Some predators adapted. Water rats learned to eat only the hearts and livers. 102 toads became hundreds of millions.

description:
What if 102 toads were released to fight a beetle?
In 1935 Australia did it, and the toads ignored the beetles and spread across the continent.
